en: How many times does the chorus repeat in your favorite song?
zh: 你最喜歡的歌曲裡，副歌部分重複幾次?

en: And, take a moment to think, how many times have you listened to it?
zh: 花點時間想想這副歌部分，你聽過幾次?

en: Chances are you've heard that chorus repeated dozens, if not hundreds, of times,
zh: 沒準有幾十次，甚至上百次

en: and it's not just popular songs in the West that repeat a lot.
zh: 而且不只是在西方流行歌有多次副歌的重複

en: Repetition is a feature that music from cultures around the world tends to share.
zh: 重複性是來自世界各地文化中的音樂所有的一項共同特點

en: So, why does music rely so heavily on repetition?
zh: 為什麼音樂如此重視重複性?

en: One part of the answer come from what psychologists call the mere-exposure effect.
zh: 一部分原因來自心理學家所謂的單純曝光效應

notes.example: How come you didn't text me back?

en: In short, people tend to prefer things they've been exposed to before.
zh: 總之，人們傾向於喜歡他們接觸過的東西

en: For example, a song comes on the radio that we don't particularly like,
zh: 例如，收音機播放不怎麼喜愛的歌

en: but then we hear the song at the grocery store, at the movie theater and again on the street corner.
zh: 但後來在雜貨店、電影院、街角，持續聽到這首歌

en: Soon, we are tapping to the beat, singing the words, even downloading the track.
zh: 很快地，我們會擊打節拍、唱出歌詞甚至下載這首歌

en: This mere-exposure effect doesn't just work for songs.
zh: 單純曝光效應不限於歌曲

en: It also works for everything from shapes to Super Bowl ads.
zh: 也適用於每樣事物，從形狀到超級盃廣告

en: So, what makes repetition so uniquely prevalent in music?
zh: 為何重複性會在音樂中如此獨特地凸顯出來?

en: To investigate, psychologists asked people to listen to musical compositions that avoided exact repetition.
zh: 為了研究這個問題，心理學家請實驗對象聽不完全相同但重複的音樂

en: They heard excerpts from these pieces in either their original form,
zh: 聽到的音樂片段是原版的

en: or in a version that had been digitally altered to include repetition.
zh: 或是以電子更改加入重複的版本

en: Although the original versions had been composed by some of the most respected 20th century composers,
zh: 雖然原版的音樂來自一些20世紀的知名作曲家

en: and the repetitive versions had been assembled by brute force audio editing,
zh: 而重複性版本是由音頻編輯強制組成

en: people rated the repetitive versions as more enjoyable, more interesting
zh: 實驗對象認為重複性版本比較好聽、有趣

en: and more likely to have been composed by a human artist.
zh: 更有可能是真人作曲家之作

en: Musical repetition is deeply compelling.
zh: 重複性音樂十分引人入勝

en: Think about the Muppets classic, "Mahna Mahna."
zh: 想想經典「大青蛙劇場」中的歌 《Mahna Mahna》

en: If you've heard it before, it's almost impossible after I sing, "Mahna mahna," not to respond, "Do doo do do do."
zh: 你如果聽過在我唱了《Mahna Mahna》 幾乎一定會以《Do doo do do do》回應

en: Repetition connects each bit of music irresistibly to the next bit of music that follows it.
zh: 重複性將一段音樂引誘性地連接到下一段

en: So when you hear a few notes, you're already imagining what's coming next.
zh: 所以當你聽到幾個音符你已經想像到接下來的音符

en: Your mind is unconsciously singing along, and without noticing, you might start humming out loud.
zh: 在心裡不經意的唱著而在不知不覺中可能開始哼出聲

en: Recent studies have shown that when people hear a segment of music repeated, they are more likely to move or tap along to it.
zh: 近期研究顯示，當人們重複聽到一段音樂他們較有可能隨著律動或敲擊

en: Repetition invites us into music as imagined participants, rather than as passive listeners.
zh: 重複性邀請我們進入音樂成為想像中的參予者而不是被動的聽眾

en: Research has also shown that listeners shift their attention across musical repetitions,
zh: 研究報告也顯示在音樂重複時，聽者轉移注意力

notes.zh: run across someone：偶然遇見某人
notes.example: I ran across an old friend at the bookstore.

en: focusing on different aspects of the sound on each new listen.
zh: 在每次重複中，專注聲音的不同面

en: You might notice the melody of a phrase the first time,
zh: 第一次聽，你可能只注意到一句旋律

en: but when it's repeated, your attention shifts to how the guitarist bends a pitch.
zh: 但當旋律重複時，你會將注意力轉移到吉他手如何塑造一個音調

en: This also occurs in language, with something called semantic satiation.
zh: 這相當於語言中的 「語義飽食」

en: Repeating a word like atlas ad nauseam can make you stop thinking about what the word means,
zh: 不斷地重複一個詞，比如 atlas (地圖集)，ad nauseam (令人作嘔) 能讓你停止思考這個字的意義

en: and instead focus on the sounds: the odd way the "L" follows the "T."
zh: 而專注於聲音: “T” 奇怪地連接著 ”L” 聲

en: In this way, repetition can open up new worlds of sound not accessible on first hearing.
zh: 如此，重複性能開啟一個新地聲音世界一個在初次試聽時無法觸及地世界

en: The "L" following the "T" might not be aesthetically relevant to "atlas,"
zh: “T” 接著 “L” 對於 “atlas” 可能沒有審美性的關聯

en: but the guitarist pitch bending might be of critical expressive importance.
zh: 但吉他手的音調塑造可能具有關鍵的表達重要性

en: The speech to song illusion captures how simply repeating a sentence a number of times shifts listeners attention
zh: 語音到歌曲的錯覺是簡單的抓到多次重複一個句子，將聽眾的注意力

en: to the pitch and temporal aspects of the sound, so that the repeated spoken language
zh: 轉移到聲音的音調和時序讓重複的口語

en: actually begins to sound like it is being sung.
zh: 果真聽起來像是被唱出來的

notes.example: Actually, we're just looking around for now.

en: A similar effect happens with random sequences of sound.
zh: 聲音的隨機序列有類似的效果

notes.example: Participants were assigned to groups at random.

en: People will rate random sequences they've heard on repeated loop as more musical than a random sequence they've only heard once.
zh: 重複聽過的隨機序列將被公定比只聽過一次的隨機序列更具音樂性

notes.example: Participants were assigned to groups at random.

en: Repetition gives rise to a kind of orientation to sound
zh: 重複性給予聲音一種方針

en: that we think of as distinctively musical, where we're listening along with the sound,
zh: 使我們認為是有獨特音樂性的，讓我們聽到聲音時

en: engaging imaginatively with the note about to happen.
zh: 用想像力參與將要出現的音符

en: This mode of listening ties in with our susceptibility to musical ear worms, where segments of music burrow into our head,
zh: 這種聆聽形態連結於我們對音樂耳蟲的感受性有音樂片段鑽入腦中

en: and play again and again, as if stuck on repeat.
zh: 彷彿停留在一遍又一遍的播放

en: Critics are often embarrassed by music's repetitiveness, finding it childish or regressive,
zh: 評論家常對音樂中的重複性感到介意覺得這幼稚或具退步性的

en: but repetition, far from an embarrassment, is actually a key feature
zh: 但重複性，不是值得羞愧的事，而是一個關鍵地特點

notes.example: Actually, we're just looking around for now.

en: that gives rise to the kind of experience we think about as musical.
zh: 讓我們擁有那種所謂音樂性的體驗
